body.statement: Derive, rather than posit, a finite correction-order map \(q(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d)\), a finite family of distance resolutions, and signed weights for \(\mathfrak H_P\) whose separate propensity and control-regression vanishing moments leave bias at most \((h_n^*/(k_n^*)^{1/d})^{\alpha+\beta}\) and whose Hoeffding components are at most the variance term in \(r_n^*\), uniformly on every compact \(K\subset(0,\infty)^3\) whenever \(P_n=1\). Determine the smallest such order and exhibit a derived nonempty open set \(U\subset(0,\infty)^3\setminus\mathcal R_{\mathrm{bank}}\) with \(U\cap(\{\beta>\alpha\}\cup\{\alpha>1\})\neq\varnothing\) on which the construction works. The scheme must remain total under empty cells and singular empirical local Grams and must not estimate \(f_P\).
body.justification: The correction order and enlarged asymmetric smoothness frontier are the genuinely open mathematical content of the sparse-local branch.
body.gap: The banked first-difference identity works only on \(0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\); Dobriban et al. remove polynomial trends for homoskedastic variance, not the two unequally smooth causal nuisances in a local \(R\)-ratio.
body.consumer: A solution gives an implementable density-free estimator for sparse local windows, including a region with reversed nuisance ordering or propensity smoothness above one.
